title: Called to the police station for questioning
triggers: police called me to the station
got a notice from police to appear
police want to question my mother at the station

rights.plain_explanation: Where arrest isn't required, police issue a notice to appear instead. If you keep complying with the notice, you aren't arrested for that offence unless the officer records reasons.
Women, boys under 15, men over 60, and people with a disability or acute illness can't be made to come to the station as witnesses. They're questioned where they live, unless they choose to go.

do_now: Ask for the notice in writing and keep a copy.
Go at the time given, ideally with a lawyer or a trusted person.
If you're a woman, a child or a senior, you can ask to be questioned at home.
user_at_fault_cases: Ignoring a valid notice to appear can lead to arrest, so do respond to it.

escalation.label: Free legal aid
escalation.detail: Call NALSA on 15100 or visit your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at the district court. Women, children, people in custody and people below the income limit get a free lawyer.
